step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram visually depicts user interactions with a mobile application and other devices, flowing into an AWS AppSync layer, which in turn orchestrates with DynamoDB and Lambda functions. A legacy system on EC2 interacts with Aurora and Couchbase, and feeds into DynamoDB. Fargate processes content relevance, updating DynamoDB. RedShift serves as an analytics platform, pulling data from DynamoDB, Aurora, and Couchbase, and triggering another Lambda function to update DynamoDB with rankings. Edges are established based on explicit arrows shown in the whiteboard diagram and confirmed by the transcript where necessary for flow sequencing.

graph.name: MusicMatch Architecture
graph.notes: MusicMatch's architecture focuses on real-time content synchronization and user feedback processing. It leverages AWS AppSync for real-time data, DynamoDB for task management, and integrates with a legacy EC2 system. Fargate, RedShift, and Lambda are used for background content processing, analytics, and task orchestration, enhancing the user's music experience with synchronized lyrics and translations.

nodes.name: Mobile App User
nodes.notes: Users consuming music content and providing feedback via the MusicMatch mobile application.

nodes.name: Community/Users
nodes.notes: Community members providing feedback, edits, and translations for song lyrics and content.

nodes.name: Internal/Experts
nodes.notes: Internal MusicMatch staff or domain experts responsible for content editing and quality control tasks.

nodes.name: AppSync
nodes.notes: Provides a real-time data synchronization and API layer for client applications, distributing tasks and handling content submission.

nodes.name: Legacy MusicMatch
nodes.notes: Hosts the initial, legacy part of the MusicMatch backend, processing incoming feedback.

nodes.name: Editorial Data
nodes.notes: Relational database storing editorial content, such as curated lyrics and translations.

nodes.name: User-Generated Data (Couchbase)
nodes.notes: NoSQL open-source database (Couchbase) used for storing user-generated content and data.

nodes.name: Task Management
nodes.notes: Stores tasks generated from user feedback and content updates, which are then distributed and managed.

nodes.name: Task Orchestration Lambda
nodes.notes: Orchestrates complex operations, such as simultaneous writing of task results to DynamoDB and content publication, triggered by AppSync.

nodes.name: Content Ranker
nodes.notes: Runs batch jobs to update and prioritize content based on input like streaming service rankings, contributing to task relevance.

nodes.name: Analytics Platform
nodes.notes: Data warehouse for analytics, extracting classifications of the most relevant content per country and language.

nodes.name: Ranking Contributor Lambda
nodes.notes: Processes content rankings extracted from RedShift, contributing to the overall ranking of tasks stored in DynamoDB.
